answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity lock a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so a gale of fake accounts becomes expensive instead of free. New identities must also wander through a slow probation where they earn reputation only by completing real, verifiable work, while a plume of sudden identical signups from one source triggers manual review. Forging thousands of agents then costs real money and time, far more than the rewards they could harvest.
